data.title: Doxepin (oral + topical)
data.summary: Antihistamines · Tricyclic antidepressant with very potent H1 and H2 receptor blocking activity
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** Tricyclic antidepressant with very potent H1 and H2 receptor blocking activity

## Mechanism of action
- H1 affinity about 800 times diphenhydramine and 50 times hydroxyzine; also H2 blockade, anticholinergic, sedative and antidepressant (noradrenaline/serotonin reuptake inhibition)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic urticaria (especially with anxiety/depression, nocturnal itch), cold urticaria, dermographism
- Neuropathic itch and pain, psychogenic excoriation, lichen simplex chronicus
- Topical 5% cream: itch of atopic dermatitis and lichen simplex (short courses)

## Dose & formulations
- Oral: 10–25 mg at bedtime (up to 75 mg/day); elderly 10 mg
- Topical 5% cream: four times daily for up to 8 days, maximum 10% body surface

## Adverse effects
- Sedation, dry mouth, constipation, weight gain, orthostatic hypotension
- Cardiac arrhythmia (QT prolongation), lethal in overdose
- Topical: drowsiness from absorption (about 20%), allergic contact dermatitis (common), burning

## Contraindications
- Recent MI, heart block, narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, MAO inhibitors within 14 days, mania

## Drug interactions
- CYP2D6 inhibitors (fluoxetine, terbinafine) raise levels; alcohol; other serotonergic drugs

## Monitoring
- ECG in older patients or cardiac history

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (neonatal withdrawal, limited data).

## Viva points
- Most potent H1 blocker available
- Topical doxepin: absorbed enough to cause drowsiness; frequent contact allergy

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.32 and ch.35; Khopkar (Antihistamines; topical doxepin). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
